grader.finalMessage:
The Opus 5.5 (high) MCP Guided run (`2026-10-08_0857_mcp-guided_opus-5.5-high`) scores **98/100**. All 43 automated checks passed, the grade appears in the report table, the solution is archived, and `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35/35 |
| Content modeling | 25/25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 25/25 |
| Content & presentation | 9/10 |
| Process & honesty | 4/5 |

**Summary:** A complete MCP-built blog that follows every project convention:
- three reusable blocks: rich text, image and quote
- clean front page and post types, filed in the right folders
- two published posts about MCP, using the provided Unsplash photos
- a polished Tailwind layout
- every block rendered through a small adapter that hands off to its own ViewComponent, as `AGENTS.md` requires

The build has 0 warnings, the domain `/` is on the front page, and every page is published.

**Issues (both minor):**
- **Wrote outside the project folder.** It saved its curl page checks to `/tmp/page*.html`, then deleted them. The automated `process.stayedInFolder` check missed this; the model disclosed it in its own final report. That costs 1 point in process.
- **Short posts.** Each post has 4 blocks and about 5–6 paragraphs. That meets the brief but is on the short side, so content lost 1 point, the same as earlier runs with short posts. I first scored content 10/10 and lowered it to 9 to match how those runs were graded.

The final report was accurate and candid. It disclosed the cancelled bulk publish, the data type folder it couldn't check (it turned out correct), and the `/tmp` breach.

Files are in `results/2026-10-08_0857_mcp-guided_opus-5.5-high/`:
- `grade.json`
- `grade.md`
